metric_model: CHAOSS AI Alignment - Community Governed Use

scope.note: Scoring confined to the files named on the command line; 'no' means not addressed in those files.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies to Pull Requests, Issues, and comments on issues/PRs; disclosure required when AI generated 'a significant portion' of the contribution (beyond simple autocomplete)
domains.accountability_wording: The human contributor is the sole party responsible for the contribution.

evidence.quote: The human contributor is the sole party responsible for the contribution.
You must fully understand every line of code in the submission.
If AI was used to generate a significant portion of your contribution (i.e. beyond simple autocomplete), we require you to disclose it in the Pull Request description.
Do not post comments on issues or PRs that are AI-generated.

domains.reasoning: The policy directly and repeatedly names PRs, issues, and comments, sets explicit supervision requirements (human must understand and explain the code, disclose AI use in commit trailer), and assigns the contributor as sole responsible party. This is the core, most fully specified domain in the document.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no scope limit; no accountability holder named
domains.reasoning: The policy contains no reference to meeting recording, notetaker bots, or capture of discussion/small-group content of any kind.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: documentation submitted as part of a Pull Request only; blogs and design assets outside the PR/code process are not mentioned
domains.accountability_wording: The human contributor is the sole party responsible for the contribution.

evidence.quote: If you submit a Pull Request that includes AI-generated code, documentation, or comments:

domains.suggested_improvement: no scope for blogs/design assets outside PR documentation
domains.reasoning: Documentation is named, but only in the narrow context of a Pull Request submission alongside code; the general 'content' domain (blog posts, design assets, standalone docs work) is never named or governed separately.

domains.rationale_only_mention: We seek to use our time and resources effectively.
domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no accountability holder named for moderation use of AI
domains.reasoning: The policy discusses maintainer time/overhead as a rationale for restricting low-effort AI contributions, but never addresses AI use in moderation actions themselves (e.g. AI-assisted banning, content takedowns, or user sanctions).

domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on maintainers/reviewers using AI to review contributions
domains.reasoning: The one clause referencing 'code review' bars the contributor from copy-pasting to/from a chatbot while answering reviewer questions - this concerns contributor conduct during review, not whether a reviewer or AI tool may perform the review itself. No statement addresses AI used by a human or agent to review a contribution.

domains.scope_or_volume_limits: Applies specifically to submitting Pull Requests

evidence.quote: Autonomous AI agents may not submit Pull Requests to Mastodon repositories.

domains.suggested_improvement: no accountability holder stated for autonomous/agentic use
domains.reasoning: The ban on autonomous agents submitting PRs is explicit and clearly named, but the policy assigns no accountability holder specifically for this domain (the general contributor-accountability clause is framed around human submissions, not agent-initiated ones).

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no rule on environmental impact stated
domains.reasoning: No text in the policy discusses energy use, water use, carbon footprint, or hardware footprint of AI tools.

domains.suggested_improvement: no supervision level; no rule on server load or hardware cost
domains.reasoning: The policy mentions maintainer time and resource constraints as rationale for restricting low-effort AI PRs, but this concerns human moderation/review load, not server load or hardware financing. No infrastructure-specific statement exists.

domains.rationale_only_mention: If AI was used, the resulting code does not violate the terms of service of the AI provider and does not include "regurgitated" code from libraries with incompatible licences
domains.suggested_improvement: no statement on the project's own data being used to train models
domains.reasoning: The copyright/legal section is concerned with AI models potentially having been trained on third-party code that ends up regurgitated into a contribution - a provenance/copyright concern about incoming code, not about whether Mastodon's own user data, issues, or discussions may be used to train AI models. The latter is never addressed.

consent_policy_specificity.overall_posture: The policy is highly specific and restrictive about code_contributions (PRs, issues, comments) - requiring human understanding, disclosure, and sole contributor accountability - and explicitly bans autonomous agent PR submissions, but it never names or governs notetaker bots, moderation, AI-assisted review, environmental impact, infrastructure strain, or the project's own data being used for training; content (documentation) is touched only incidentally within the PR context.

awaiting_implementation.specific_tools_in_use: Awaiting implementation: named-product detection beyond known file signatures
awaiting_implementation.ai_tool_owner: Awaiting implementation: ownership and data control
awaiting_implementation.environmental_footprint: Awaiting implementation: model/system card and ESG disclosure
awaiting_implementation.proportionality: Awaiting implementation: resource use relative to contributor count (needs platform usage data)

use_composition_partial.note: Detection only. Absence of signal is not absence of use.

policy_change.blocker: Draft classifier not wired in or validated against hand-graded history. Repo.history() and Repo.commit_patch() supply the diffs.

use_compliance.blocker: Derived metric. Requires disclosed-use data (Use Composition) checked against the specificity grid. Composition is only partially detectable, so the comparison is not yet sound.

misuse.blocker: Not automatable. CHAOSS marks the core signals unknown: text-based AI detectors are unreliable, and license-laundering and wrongful-accusation incidents need maintainer self-report.
